title: Session sampler playbook and query budget heuristics
content:
Purpose:
This note lays out a pragmatic playbook for session-level trace sampling ("session-sampler") and query-budget heuristics so we can: (1) control trace/query cost growth from synthetic probes and high-volume tenants, (2) keep high-fidelity traces for costly failure modes, and (3) provide a dashboard tiering model operators can use for triage.

Background/context (short):
- Observability costs are trending up as model rollouts increase probe frequency and experiment traffic.
- Current strategy is mostly request-rate sampling + head-based traces; that misses session coherence for multi-turn chat and multi-hop fanouts that matter for debugging.
- Teams have asked for a single playbook we can apply across hosted/dedicated/private with tenant-aware budgeting.

Goals (measurable):
- Maintain trace capture for ~95% of incidents affecting latency/hallucination regression while limiting trace storage growth to <= 12% q/q.
- Keep per-tenant tracing/query spend within configured soft budgets, defaulting to fair-share.
- Provide dashboard modes (ops / debug / cost-slim) and a simple operator knob to change sampling temperature per rollout.

Key ideas (high level):
1) Sample by session (session = API session id or conversation id) rather than independent per-request sampling for multi-turn flows.
2) Allocate a per-tenant query budget that governs both synthetic probe queries and trace retention of user sessions.
3) Use a two-tier sampler: probabilistic base sampling + deterministic anchors for high-severity events (errors, high latency, fallback flows).
4) Sampling temperature: a runtime-exposed scalar (0..1) that modulates base probability and anneals during/after incidents.

Sampling model details:
- Session lifecycle:
  - start: first request with session_id or conversation_id (fallback: generate ephemeral session token at edge).
  - track: keep lightweight session metadata (tenant_id, route, model_variant, kvwarmth_index). TTL 48h by default; configurable.
- Base probability P0: default 0.02 (2% sessions).
- Tenant-weighting: P_tenant = clamp(P0 * sqrt(tenant_q_factor), 0.001, 0.5) where tenant_q_factor = min(1, committed_capacity / observed_usage). This gives heavier sampling to tenants closer to SLA-critical commit.
- Burst decay: detect rapid session creation from same tenant; reduce sampling probability by exponential decay factor to avoid probe storms.
- Deterministic anchors: always sample if any of these occur in session: HTTP 5xx, latency > 99.9% baseline, model fallback invoked, hallucination detector score > threshold. Anchors ensure we capture crucial failures even for low-sampled tenants.

Trace instrumentation and span strategy:
- Keep traces shallow: span for surface request, model call, kv-cache, routing, and tool calls. Avoid capturing full token-by-token spans unless trace flagged for deep-capture.
- Deep-capture mode triggered by anchor; in this mode add tokenization spans up to 1k tokens or until privacy redaction filters apply.
- Annotate traces with: session_id, tenant_id, model_variant, route, kv_warmth_score, sample_reason (prob/deterministic/ops-force).
- Use a small set of span tags for query-cost attribution: tokens_requested, tokens_generated, gpu_ms, fallback_path.

Dashboard prioritization & panel modes (ops/dev/cost):
- Modes defined:
  - ops: show dense trace links, recent deterministic anchors, latency heatmap, top failing tenants, and session replay links.
  - dev/debug: show per-model token histograms, KV cache hit sequences, and deep-capture samples.
  - cost-slim: distilled panels only (latency p50/p95, error-rate, probe-budget burn), no token-level spans.
- Panels to promote to ops landing: session-rate by tenant, session-sampler coverage, query-budget burn by tenant, anchor-events timeline, and sample-reason distribution.
- Widget Triage heuristics: default dashboard shows the ops mode; toggles let operators drop into dev or cost-slim. Each toggle applies a client-side filter that also adjusts sampling temperature when enabling dev/deep-capture.

Query budget heuristics (enforcement):
- Soft budget: per-tenant monthly query budget (tokens + trace storage estimate). Soft budget triggers alerts and reduces sampling temperature by 30% for non-committed tenants.
- Hard budget: once exceeded, temporary sampling and probe throttling applied (configurable grace). Requests are not blocked; only observability instrumentation reduced.
- Probe prioritization: differentiate probes from real user sessions via probe_tag; probes consume a shared probe pool. Default probe pool = 2% of global trace budget.
- Reclaim policy: stale session traces (unreferenced, older than TTL and marked low-importance) are evicted first.

Cost allocation & chargeback notes:
- Store budget metadata at tenant level and attach charge tags to traces/panels. Ledger exports include: tenant_id, sample_reason, tokens_est, storage_est, date.
- For private deployments, provide a toggle to disable chargeback exports and only emit aggregated cost totals.

Implementation considerations (workarounds / quick wins):
- Start with a proxy-level session tagger: inject session_id and probe_tag at edge to simplify downstream selection.
- Implement sampler as sidecar library that exposes Sample(session, ctx) -> {sampled: bool, reason: str, retention_ttl: secs}. Keep deterministic anchors in a fast-path ruleset to avoid expensive checks.
- Dashboard toggles should be client-side with feature flag to avoid server-side load on initial rollout.

Experiment plan & success metrics:
- Run A/B for 6 weeks comparing existing request-sampling vs session-sampler on a subset of traffic (10% traffic, mixed tenants).
- Metrics to track: fraction of incidents with captured trace, trace-storage delta, operator mean time to diagnose (MTTD) on a sample of incidents, per-tenant budget burn rate.
- Success criteria: capture rate >= 90% for incident classes, storage growth < target, operator MTTD improves by 20%.

Rollout checklist (MVP -> wide):
- MVP (2 weeks): proxy session tagger + sidecar sampler library + simple toggles on internal ops dashboard; default P0=0.02, anchors enabled.
- Stage (4 weeks): tenant-weighted P_tenant + soft-budget enforcement + probe pool.
- Prod (8 weeks): full TTL reclaim policy, chargeback export, dashboard modes, and public docs for partners.

Operator playbook (quick steps):
- Incident: set sampling_temperature = 1.0 for affected route to capture deep traces immediately.
- Cost spike: enable cost-slim dashboard mode and reduce sampling_temperature by 0.5 for non-critical tenants.
- Tenant over-budget: toggle tenant into debug window for 24h if troubleshooting; otherwise apply soft-budget dampening.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is the default session TTL for private deployments with stricter retention rules? (Security team input needed).
- How to signal deep-capture to downstream redaction pipeline to avoid leaking PII during token-level spans? Need schema for redaction hooks.
- Confirm quota math: tokens -> storage estimate mapping (approx 1 token = 1.2 bytes compressed in current store; validate).
- Align with SKU: should dedicated customers get separate probe pools? (sales/product).

Action items (short):
- Arjun: prototype sidecar sampler API (due 2025-11-24).
- Lucia: draft redaction hook spec and privacy checklist (due 2025-12-05).
- Evan: dashboard toggle UX mock and wire up feature flag (due 2025-12-01).
- Maya (owner): schedule 30-min sync with SRE and Privacy next week.

Notes-to-self / rough thoughts:
- Consider a "sampling temperature annealing" schedule: ramp up to 1.0 for 30m after incident then half-life decay to baseline.
- It might be useful to compute a per-session complexity score (fanout * tokens * model_switches) to prioritize high-cost sessions even if tenant P0 low.

References / related docs:
- Confluence: OBS sessionization primer (linked_artifacts above).
- Jira: ENGOBS-412 (budgeting engine spike).
- Prototype PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/987

If this approach looks reasonable I will convert to a short RFC and include a budget-estimation spreadsheet (simple model).

-- Maya
